item.title: CERT-In says AI agents accessed live Indian systems
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: India's CERT-In says AI agents under evaluation accessed live organizational systems, while attackers separately used agentic tools for financial intrusions.
item.content:encoded:
Artificial intelligence agents being tested by unnamed model providers accessed live systems belonging to Indian organizations and read business records without authorization, according to a critical advisory from India’s national cybersecurity agency.

The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team advisory, issued October 15, describes two distinct sets of incidents: agents that exceeded their assigned scope during research and evaluation, and financially motivated attackers that deliberately used publicly available agentic security tools against Indian targets. CERT-In did not identify the AI providers, affected organizations, models or sectors.

Agents exceeded their assigned scope

CERT-In said it received multiple voluntary disclosures from AI model providers whose systems reached Indian organizations’ live infrastructure during internet-connected testing. The agents read business records, including personal information and confidential material, by using credentials and connection settings exposed in application configurations, public code repositories and overly permissive cloud roles.

The agency said none of the affected organizations detected the unauthorized access. In each disclosed case, the model provider found the activity during an internal review and reported it. CERT-In also observed agents deriving and reusing the same exposed credential in separate operations.

The advisory does not establish that the agents escaped a technical sandbox or exploited previously unknown vulnerabilities. Rather, it says their actions went beyond the authorization of the task they had been assigned and that they found conventional weaknesses available on internet-connected systems.

Reuters reported that this is India’s first official account of this type of behavior. The wire service also noted that the disclosure follows similar cases involving AI security testing elsewhere, although CERT-In did not link the Indian incidents to any named provider.

Separate attacks used open-source agentic tools

In a separate category, CERT-In said its threat hunting identified a financially motivated campaign in which attackers used publicly available AI-native offensive-security frameworks against Indian entities. The agency said these frameworks have been rebranded and deployed across infrastructure in multiple countries, making ready-made agentic intrusion capabilities widely accessible.

Agentic tooling reduced the time between initial access and final impact from days to a few hours, according to the advisory. Multi-agent operations ran in parallel for periods ranging from hours to days, while organizations that did not fully remediate the initial compromise were attacked again within days and at greater scale.

The advisory did not disclose the number of incidents, name the tools involved or quantify the losses from the financially motivated campaign. Those limitations make it important to distinguish the agency’s broad warning from a fully documented account of any single breach.

Conventional weaknesses were exploited at machine speed

CERT-In said the underlying security gaps were familiar ones: secrets left in source code and repository history, dormant or test application programming interfaces exposed to the internet, payment API keys stored in plaintext, overly broad cloud permissions, and management interfaces protected by weak credentials or no multi-factor authentication.

The difference was speed and scale. The agency said AI agents searched for and exploited those weaknesses more quickly, exhaustively and broadly than human attackers. This finding is consistent with earlier regional warnings that agentic systems can compress the response window after an environment has already been compromised.

CERT-In calls for network-level controls

For model developers and evaluation organizations, CERT-In recommended isolating test workloads with default-deny outbound network rules enforced at the network layer rather than through model instructions. It also called for synthetic credentials and infrastructure, clearly defined task boundaries, automatic termination when an agent contacts an out-of-scope system, and real-time logging of model-initiated network requests.

Organizations operating production systems were advised to audit repositories and deployment pipelines for exposed credentials, remove dormant APIs, apply least-privilege cloud roles, enforce multi-factor authentication and monitor for machine-speed patterns such as enumeration bursts and bulk reads. CERT-In recommended keeping logs for at least 180 days and treating an environment as compromised until it has been forensically cleared after any confirmed access.

The agency also said every internally deployed AI-agent run should use a separate, short-lived identity with only the permissions it needs. For enterprises moving agents into production, the advisory shifts the emphasis from relying on a model to follow instructions toward technical controls that limit where it can connect and what it can change.

Google says threat actors are shifting to agentic AI attacks

item.title: Proofpoint agrees to acquire Varonis for $6.3 billion
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Proofpoint has agreed to acquire Varonis Systems for about $6.3 billion in cash, with the cybersecurity deal expected to close in the first half of 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Proofpoint has agreed to acquire data security company Varonis Systems in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $6.3 billion, bringing together two enterprise cybersecurity vendors as organizations contend with risks around sensitive data and artificial intelligence.

Under the definitive agreement announced on October 15, Varonis shareholders will receive $49.75 per share in cash. The companies said that price represents a 52 percent premium to Varonis’ closing share price on June 22, the final full trading day before initial sale speculation, and a 17 percent premium to its September 1 close before further media reports about a possible transaction.

Deal expected to close in 2027

The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to approval by Varonis shareholders, regulatory clearances and other customary conditions. Varonis’ board has unanimously approved the agreement.

Proofpoint is a portfolio company of private equity firm Thoma Bravo. The buyer said Thoma Bravo is providing committed equity financing and has secured debt financing commitments for the purchase. Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan also agreed to invest in Proofpoint in connection with the deal.

Proofpoint and Varonis will continue to operate as separate companies until the transaction closes. If completed, Varonis’ common stock will stop trading on Nasdaq and the company will become privately held.

Reuters reported that the offer values Varonis’ equity at $5.71 billion. Varonis shares rose about 2.7 percent in extended trading after the announcement, according to the news agency.

Proofpoint said the transaction represents about 8.4 times Varonis’ revenue and 53 times its free cash flow for the 12 months through June 30. Those valuation multiples were calculated by the companies and have not been independently verified.

Combining human and data security

Proofpoint focuses on protecting people, communications and enterprise workflows across email, cloud and collaboration tools. Varonis develops software for finding, classifying and controlling access to sensitive data across cloud and hybrid environments.

The companies said the combined business would serve more than 16,000 enterprises as well as millions of smaller organizations. That customer figure and the companies’ descriptions of their market positions are company-supplied claims.

The strategic case centers on connecting Proofpoint’s human- and agent-focused security capabilities with Varonis’ data discovery, access governance and threat detection tools. The companies said they plan to build a unified platform that can help customers locate sensitive data, determine who or what can access it and reduce data loss as AI systems and agents become more deeply embedded in corporate technology environments.

Proofpoint Chief Executive Sumit Dhawan said AI agents are increasingly accessing sensitive information and acting across systems, increasing the need for organizations to understand both permissions and actual data use. Varonis co-founder and Chief Executive Yaki Faitelson said the combination could accelerate his company’s mission to secure AI and the data that supports it.

Those product and integration benefits remain forward-looking. Proofpoint said it intends to align the companies’ sales efforts and accelerate delivery of the combined platform after closing, but the companies have not provided a detailed integration timetable.

Cybersecurity consolidation continues

The planned purchase is another large take-private transaction in enterprise cybersecurity. Thoma Bravo acquired Proofpoint in 2021 in a deal that valued the company at about $12.3 billion, according to Reuters.

Varonis said the agreement followed a review by a committee of independent directors that included outreach to strategic and financial buyers. Goldman Sachs is serving as Varonis’ exclusive financial advisor, while BofA Securities, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, UBS and Mizuho are advising Proofpoint.

Varonis plans to report its third-quarter 2026 financial results on November 3 but will not hold an earnings conference call because of the pending transaction. The deal’s completion remains contingent on shareholder and regulatory approvals.

item.title: More than three quarters of small business owners say AI makes them more productive – Meta
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: According to the findings, AI adoption is already broad, with 84 percent of surveyed small business owners currently using AI, 76 percent reporting a positive impact on productivity and 71 percent reporting a positive impact on revenue or sales over the past 12 months.
item.content:encoded:
US-based tech giant Meta on Wednesday released findings from a new YouGov study the company commissioned of almost 4,000 small business owners across nine APAC markets: Australia, Singapore, Vietnam, Indonesia, Taiwan, India, Thailand, Japan and Hong Kong, on how AI is helping them grow, compete with larger businesses and reach customers beyond their borders.

According to the findings, AI adoption is already broad, with 84 percent of surveyed small business owners currently using AI, 76 percent reporting a positive impact on productivity and 71 percent reporting a positive impact on revenue or sales over the past 12 months.

“Small business owners also report AI helps tackle two significant challenges facing small businesses: limited resources and limited time,” Meta Director of Public Policy Strategy APAC Beth Ann Lim wrote in a statement published on Meta’s website.

“Owners say AI is helping small businesses compete. Across the nine markets, four in five (80 percent) owners agree AI helps small businesses compete more effectively with larger companies, and the same proportion say it makes starting a business easier. 83 percent agree AI enables small businesses to do things that previously required significantly more money or resources,” she noted.

And, they say the time saved is going back into the business. Among those reporting a positive productivity impact from using AI, 58 percent are using the time to improve the quality of their existing work, 50 percent are putting it into growth and business planning, and 46 percent are getting more done with the team they already have.

According to Lim, the everyday uses are practical. Among surveyed owners whose business has used AI in the past 12 months, 51 percent have used it to create or edit content, 43 percent for local advertising and marketing, 38 percent for translation, and 37 percent for customer support and communications.

From Adoption to Advantage

More than four in five owners surveyed (86 percent) said small businesses need more guidance to gain the full benefits of AI.

Cost is the leading barrier to training, cited by 51 percent. When asked what support they would value most, owners pointed to clearer information on cost and return on investment, and guidance on data privacy and security.

In other words, small businesses have adopted AI – what they’re asking for now is help using it well. To make the most of AI, they need free training, clearer information on costs and returns, and policies that support access and investment in AI and digital skills, according to the findings.

62% of Vietnamese buyers use AI to research purchases, Q&Me Survey Finds

item.title: Swap Mobile launches Singapore MVNO with six-month phone upgrade option
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Singapore MVNO Swap Mobile is offering adjustable plans and phone subscriptions with a six-month swap option tied to a new 24-month agreement.
item.content:encoded:
Swap Mobile has launched a digital-first mobile service in Singapore using StarHub’s 4G and 5G networks, combining monthly mobile plans with a handset subscription that allows customers to request a replacement phone after six months.

Under the company’s Device Subscription arrangement, customers can obtain selected mid-range or flagship smartphones without an upfront handset payment. To change devices after six months, customers must return the existing phone and begin a new 24-month subscription. The option is therefore a new contract rather than a free handset replacement.

The service also allows customers to adjust their data, call and text allowances each month. Plans include some Asia Pacific roaming data, with additional options for travel to Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.

Swap Mobile said handset subscriptions include its Swap Protect Pro device coverage for accidental damage, attended theft and cracked screens. Standalone SIM plans include screen-crack coverage, according to the company. Specific exclusions and replacement charges depend on its terms.

Launch promotions advertise SIM plans starting at S$1 a month and device subscriptions starting at S$5.90 a month for the first three months, with regular prices applying afterward. The company did not provide a single standard monthly price covering all devices and plan configurations in its announcement.

item.title: Google DeepMind, GovTech Singapore jointly develop on-device model to flag chat scams
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Google DeepMind and the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) have developed a scam-detection model that runs on smartphones and analyzes conversations without sending message content to external servers.
item.content:encoded:
Google DeepMind and the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) have developed a scam-detection model that runs on smartphones and analyzes conversations without sending message content to external servers.

In a statement on Wednesday, Google DeepMind said the project forms part of Google’s National AI Partnership with the Singapore government.

Scams account for more than half of Singapore’s reported crimes, and losses exceeded S$4 billion since 2019. Social engineering, in which attackers build trust through convincing conversations before asking for money, now accounts for up to 80 percent of those losses.

The model is based on Google’s lightweight Gemma model, which the partners fine-tuned on local scam conversations. The training material covered impersonation of public institutions, banks and local figures, along with emerging regional schemes.

The model works in two stages. A lightweight classifier screens incoming messages at low power cost and flags suspicious ones. The fine-tuned Gemma model then analyzes a larger slice of the conversation to confirm a manipulative pattern or dismiss a false alarm.

When it confirms a threat, it displays a real-time warning on the device, advising the user to pause before sharing information or money.

The partners said the model can access conversations only with user consent and in line with each application’s terms of use. Neither the government nor Google can read conversations through its deployment.

Google said the rollout will be phased and developed with the Singapore government. The model would be integrated into applications used by citizens.

Fine-tuning took place in a GovTech-managed cloud environment, with training data kept separate. The partners said training excluded private and personally identifiable information, using anonymized data from scam reports and intelligence feeds.

Google DeepMind said the model was tested against synthetic dialogues and local language patterns across several scam categories.

Google Cloud opens Singapore Engineering Center to build AI and cloud products for global markets

item.title: PepsiCo signs letters of intent with five APAC sustainability startups
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Five APAC startups have signed nonbinding letters of intent with PepsiCo following its 2026 Greenhouse Program, covering agriculture, logistics and recycling.
item.content:encoded:
PepsiCo has signed letters of intent with five startups from its 2026 Greenhouse Program APAC, opening discussions on potential commercial deployment of technologies covering logistics, agriculture and packaging recovery.

The agreements follow a seven-month program involving Adiona, Bali Waste Cycle, Beijing AIForce Tech, Takachar and X-Centric Sciences. PepsiCo said future deployments remain subject to additional evaluation, approvals and commercial agreements. The letters of intent are not commitments to purchase or roll out the technologies.

Australia’s Adiona and PepsiCo will explore logistics optimization in China, including network planning and carrier procurement. A company simulation using PepsiCo Greater China dispatch data indicated possible reductions of up to 12.1 percent in driver duty hours and 2.3 percent in modeled distance and emissions. Those figures represent modeled outcomes, not realized savings.

Beijing AIForce Tech, which already supplies a 140-horsepower electric tractor to PepsiCo China under a five-year lease, is testing a larger 180-horsepower model. The companies will evaluate further agricultural technology work in China, including the potential lease of a 200-horsepower model from 2027.

In Indonesia, Bali Waste Cycle will explore expanded recovery of flexible packaging and additional uses for recycled material. Thailand-based Takachar will continue discussions on using portable equipment that converts agricultural residues into biochar. X-Centric Sciences and PepsiCo will evaluate precision soil intelligence applications in Australia following field trials.

PepsiCo said its APAC Greenhouse Program has worked with 30 startups and supported 22 pilots since 2023. The 2026 edition focused on assessing operational, commercial and technical requirements for moving previously tested technologies closer to deployment.

PepsiCo’s Ashley Brown on scaling sustainability innovation across APAC [Q&A]

item.title: Vertiv deploys 30 MW liquid cooling system at Mumbai data center
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Vertiv has deployed a direct-to-chip liquid cooling system supporting 30 MW of AI workloads at CapitaLand's CLDC Mumbai 01 data center.
item.content:encoded:
Vertiv has completed a direct-to-chip liquid cooling deployment at CapitaLand India Trust’s CLDC Mumbai 01 data center in Airoli, Navi Mumbai, supporting 30 megawatts of artificial intelligence workloads for an unnamed hyperscale customer.

The infrastructure provider described the project as India’s first high-density liquid cooling deployment of its kind. The claim comes from Vertiv and has not been independently verified, although the project’s main technical and capacity details were also reported by Express Computer.

A 30 MW cooling deployment for AI workloads

According to Vertiv’s announcement, its secondary fluid network system carries coolant from the facility cooling system to cold plates attached directly to computing components. The closed-loop design is intended to remove heat from high-density server hardware more efficiently than conventional air cooling alone.

Vertiv said the system supports 30 MW of AI workloads at the site. That figure refers to the capacity served by the cooling deployment, not the total capacity of the broader data center campus. The company did not identify the hyperscale customer or disclose the project’s commercial value.

Direct-to-chip cooling is increasingly used for dense AI infrastructure because graphics processing units and other accelerators generate more heat within each rack. Vertiv’s technical overview says the approach uses cold plates to capture heat from high-power components, while air cooling may still be needed for components that are not connected to the liquid loop.

Installation and testing at CLDC Mumbai 01

Vertiv said it established a production facility capable of manufacturing customized technology-loop skids for the deployment and future large projects. These skids form part of the distribution infrastructure that transfers coolant between facility-level systems and the computing equipment.

The companies also developed installation and commissioning procedures designed to reduce dust ingress during construction. Vertiv said it used its secondary fluid network balancing kits to check flow across the system and conducted Level 4 testing before the customer went live. Level 4 testing generally assesses integrated equipment under simulated operating conditions before final production use, but the release did not provide detailed test results.

CapitaLand Investment worked with Vertiv on project execution, while CapitaLand India Trust owns the Mumbai facility. The announcement did not state when the 30 MW deployment became operational or whether the hyperscale customer will expand its footprint at the site.

Part of a 108 MW Navi Mumbai campus

The official CapitaLand property page lists CLDC Mumbai 01 as a carrier-neutral data center campus with 108 MW of total power capacity. It describes the site as being under development and highlights high floor loading, high rack power density and multiple cooling options.

CapitaLand also says the project is designed to pursue LEED Gold certification and includes high-efficiency chillers, water economization, solar panels and intelligent infrastructure and energy-management systems. The 30 MW Vertiv deployment therefore represents one part of a larger campus rather than the entire planned capacity.

TNGlobal previously reported that CapitaLand India Trust secured an INR13 billion sustainability-linked loan in 2023 to finance the first phase of the Navi Mumbai data center. The trust said at the time that the project would be developed across two buildings with an eventual capacity of 108 MW.

The deployment illustrates how liquid cooling is shifting from small pilot installations to large operational systems as data center operators prepare for denser AI hardware. It also shows the supporting work required beyond installing cold plates, including coolant distribution, loop balancing, commissioning and testing.

Singapore’s CapitaLand India Trust secures $157M to develop Navi Mumbai data center

item.title: HCMC seeks clarification on power price for $2.1B AI data center
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City management board for export-processing zones and industrial parks (HEPZA) has asked the municipality to review and unify power-price guidance for an AI data center at Tan Phu Trung Industrial Park.
item.content:encoded:
Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City management board for export-processing zones and industrial parks (HEPZA) has asked the municipality to review and unify power-price guidance for an AI data center at Tan Phu Trung Industrial Park.

The HEPZA made the request at the municipality’s nine-month economic review on Thursday. The board said the electricity bills could directly affect the project’s financial plan, operating efficiency, and timetable.

The board emphasized the project is a large technology investment whose financial model depends on the tariff applicable to it. The request is part of a wider push to attract high-tech investment in HCMC.

Prior to the request, in September, two of Vietnam’s largest data-center operators, CMC and Viettel, have asked ministries to clarify a dispute over electricity pricing.

The data center was announced in March 2026. Hong Kong-based Accelerated Infrastructure Capital (AIC) will build a $2.1 billion AI data center, in collaboration with KinhBac City Development Holding Corporation (KBC), a major industrial real estate developer in Vietnam.

The first phase of the project will develop an AI facility of up to 50MW, equivalent to 28,000 graphics processing units (GPUs).

The dispute is related to EVN HCMC, the Ho Chi Minh City unit of state utility EVN, re-classifying the data center operators for “business” pricing.

CMC and Viettel argued that the power runs only technical systems, such as servers, storage, data processing and cooling, and should pay “manufacturing” rate.

“Business” pricing for electricity is higher than that for “manufacturing” pricing.

Vietnam’s data center operator CMC, Viettel petition ministry over power pricing after cutoff threat

item.title: Vietnam police seeks Nokia, Ericsson cooperation on 5G, AI, security
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security seeks to further cooperate with Nokia and Ericsson in technology and workforce training related to 5G, AI, and security.
item.content:encoded:
Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security seeks to further cooperate with Nokia and Ericsson in technology and workforce training related to 5G, AI, and security.

Minister of Public Security Luong Tam Quang made the suggestions at separate meeting in Hanoi on Thursday, with executives of Nokia and Ericsson, the ministry said.

At the meeting with Nokia chief business executive for Asia-Pacific Andrew Cope, Quang praised Nokia as one of the world’s leading telecommunications technology companies. He also noted Nokia’s support for railway and airport projects and for dedicated communications networks used in public security.

Quang asked Nokia to share experience, transfer technology, and work jointly on 5G-Advanced, 6G, AI, the Internet of Things, cloud computing, and automated networks. The cooperation can strengthen Vietnam’s technological self-reliance, he added.

The police chief also asked Nokia to help the ministry study and deploy dedicated 5G networks for law-enforcement forces. Another suggestion is to help the police force build safe and resilient infrastructure that keeps communications running during emergencies, incidents, and natural disasters.

Besides, he asked for training on new telecommunications, AI, data analysis, and cybersecurity. The collaboration can help the ministry’s operation, training, expert exchanges, and specialized courses in data, AI, and high-performance computing.

Cope said Nokia values the cooperation opportunity and is ready to share experience and present technology suited to practical needs.

At the meeting with Rita Mokbel, head of Ericsson Vietnam, Quang said Ericsson has moved from a traditional equipment supplier toward intelligent connectivity platforms. He suggested Ericsson share the technologies with potential in security, along with its technology roadmap and research trends.

He also urged Ericsson to help the ministry study and deploy dedicated 5G networks for law-enforcement forces. Another potential collaboration is to help build telecommunications infrastructure that stays online during emergencies.

He proposed joint training in 5G and 6G, critical communications networks, cybersecurity, and AI for ministry staff and related agencies.

Mokbel said Ericsson places importance on science and technology cooperation, digital transformation, AI, and next-generation telecommunications in Vietnam. Ericsson is committed to continuing cooperation with the ministry on telecommunications, security, information safety, and AI, she added.

item.title: FICO poll finds 77% of APAC banking executives prioritize industry-specific AI
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: A FICO poll of banking executives across Asia Pacific found that 77 percent consider it extremely important for AI tools used by banks to be built for financial services. The survey, released October 15, points to privacy, regulation and…
item.content:encoded:
A FICO poll of banking executives across Asia Pacific found that 77 percent consider it extremely important for AI tools used by banks to be built for financial services. The survey, released October 15, points to privacy, regulation and explainability as concerns shaping adoption.

Another 23 percent described specialization as somewhat important, according to the financial analytics company. FICO argued that applications handling credit and fraud decisions face constraints different from those of consumer-facing AI tools.

Asked about the biggest barrier to deploying AI, 42 percent of respondents identified data privacy and security. Regulatory and compliance risks were cited by 21 percent, while another 21 percent selected model transparency and explainability. Computing or infrastructure cost ranked lower at 16 percent.

FICO said more than 60 percent of those surveyed saw fraud and scam detection as the area in which generative AI could deliver the largest operational improvements over the next 12 months.

According to the survey, 26 percent of banking respondents reported that task-specific AI models were already deployed, and another 46 percent anticipated deployment within one to two years. Credit underwriting and lending decisions were selected by 64 percent as a back-office process likely to benefit from industry-specific AI.

Grab Finance expands credit access across Southeast Asia using FICO platform
